```sh
kafka group reset-offsets <groupId>
```

Reset a consumer group's committed offsets on one or more topics

## Arguments

| Argument  | Description |
| --------- | ----------- |
| `groupId` | group id    |

Shared options and defaults: [connection profiles, JSON output, logging and help](../../../global-options/).

## Defaults

Preview-only unless --execute is present. --topic and --to are required; --to accepts earliest or latest.

## Before you run

Stop consumers first. Preview is the default; --execute applies it. Moving backward replays records and moving forward skips records. Save the prior offsets for recovery.

## Flags

| Flag                            | Description                                           |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `--brokers <string>`            | comma-separated broker list, e.g. localhost:9092      |
| `--topic <string> (repeatable)` | topic to reset (repeatable; at least one required)    |
| `--to <string>`                 | reset target: earliest or latest                      |
| `--execute`                     | actually reset the offsets (without it, preview only) |
| `--yes`                         | confirm the reset without an interactive prompt       |

## Examples

```sh
kafka group reset-offsets my-group --topic orders --to earliest --brokers localhost:9092
kafka group reset-offsets my-group --topic orders --to earliest --execute --yes --brokers localhost:9092
```

## Output

Illustrative, abbreviated output. Empty arrays show the result envelope; actual entries, identifiers, optional fields and broker errors depend on the request and cluster.

With `--json`:

```json
{
  "topics": [
    {
      "topic": "events",
      "ok": true,
      "partitions": [
        {
          "partition": 0,
          "newOffset": "0"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Declared exit codes: `0`, `1`, `2`, `4`, `5`. See the exit-code reference for meanings.
